record.file_problem: none; the full post text is present, though the referenced plots are not reproduced with readable numeric values.
record.tranche_reason: Refines the capacity account of polysemanticity with a toy SAE result: restricting the number of active latents below the data's true L0 produces polysemantic, feature-mixing latents, while training at the true L0 recovers the features. It does not test the original overcomplete-network geometry.
record.gate_note: The post reports reconstruction comparisons and plots, but those results alone do not measure the claim versions catalogued here. The relevant results are the stated latent-to-feature alignment and polysemanticity findings at L0=1 and L0=11.
record.test_reason: On toy data with known ground-truth features, the post shows that SAE latents recover the true features only when L0 equals the true L0 (11). At L0=1 they are polysemantic mixtures. This is a specific argument that dictionary features are not canonical units independent of the L0 hyperparameter, which bears on V5. It does not bear on V2: the polysemanticity is in SAE latents under an L0 constraint, not in a network's neurons competing for capacity. The 50 orthogonal features in R100 involve no superposition.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors argue there is no real sparsity–reconstruction tradeoff: only the true L0 yields correct, monosemantic SAE features. A too-low L0 makes the SAE exploit feature correlations, and reconstruction-vs-sparsity plots can therefore prefer an incorrect, polysemantic SAE.
record.recipe_differences: A toy correlated-feature data distribution and BatchTopK sparse autoencoders are used to study L0-dependent feature recovery; this is not a reproduction of the original superposition experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported feature alignment changes between L0=1 and L0=11.

fits_no_version.finding: When SAE L0 is below the true L0, SAE latents mix correlated features to improve reconstruction ('feature hedging'). This polysemanticity comes from the dictionary method, not from the model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latent polysemanticity can be an artifact of a mis-set L0 rather than a property of the underlying representation.

record.problems: Toy model only; the supplied text gives qualitative descriptions rather than readable numerical alignment or reconstruction values. The ground-truth SAE is constructed from the true features, and no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: The post's reconstruction-versus-sparsity comparisons were not included as rows because reconstruction alone does not measure the versions tested here; numeric plot values are not present in the supplied text.

untested.parts: All of it. Features are orthogonal and fewer than dimensions (50 in R100). There is no sparsity transition or geometry analysis.
All of it. No network neurons are studied and there is no importance-based allocation.
All of it. No LLMs are studied.
Stability across seeds or dictionary sizes, completeness, and any test on a real model's activations. L0 greater than the true L0 is asserted but no result is shown.

missing.what: Reconstruction vs L0 comparison: the ground-truth SAE gets much worse reconstruction than trained SAEs at low L0. Reconstruction metrics therefore favour incorrect dictionaries. No numbers are given in the text.

missing.what: The claim that an L0 above the true L0 also fails to recover the true features. It is stated in the introduction, but no result is shown in the post.

record.verdict_notes: Toy model only, with qualitative descriptions and no numeric values for the plots. The companion paper (arXiv:2508.16560) may contain quantitative results. The reader's V2 links and labels were removed because SAE-latent mixing under an L0 constraint is not the capacity account of neuron polysemanticity.

versions.untested_parts: The toy model has 50 true features in R100, not more features than dimensions. It does not test the claimed sparsity-dependent transition or regular overlap geometry.
Tests SAE latents in a toy model, not neurons in an LLM. It does not establish that important features get dedicated dimensions while less important features share them.
The reported polysemanticity occurs under a restricted L0; no condition without capacity pressure is tested.
No LLMs or LLM feature dictionaries are tested.
The post does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of a model's representation.
The toy model uses vector features and reports cosine alignment, but does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.
